the מיתיבי baraita: אחד נותן את האבן ואחד נותן את הטיט, with R' Yosei in its seifa
anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya

props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who builds any amount is liable
R' Yirmeya: for a poor man digs a hole to hide his coins in it
R' Yirmeya: its counterpart in the Mishkan -- the curtain-sewers dug a hole to hide their needles in it
Abaye: rather, for a poor man makes the legs of a small stove to set a small pot on it
Abaye: its counterpart in the Mishkan -- those who cooked dyes for curtains whose work fell short made the legs of a small stove to set a small cauldron on it
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: rather, for a householder who has a hole in his building seals it
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: its counterpart in the Mishkan -- a board into which a worm fell: one drips lead into it and seals it
Shmuel: one who sets a stone [in place] is liable
the baraita: one sets the stone and another the mortar -- the one who sets the mortar is liable
R' Yosei [in the baraita's seifa]: even if he raised [a stone] and set it on a row of stones, he is liable
there are three [kinds of] building: the bottom [row] requires setting and earth
the middle [row] requires mortar as well
the top [row] is by mere placement

supports.gloss_en: כל שהוא למאי חזיא? -- a hole to hide coins, as the curtain-sewers' hole for their needles
כל שהוא למאי חזיא? -- the legs of a small stove, as the dye-cookers' small stove in the Mishkan
כל שהוא למאי חזיא? -- sealing a small hole, as the worm-hole in a Mishkan board sealed with lead

objections.gloss_en: כיון דמשתכי לא עבדי הכי -- since [needles] rust [in the ground], they did not do so
אין עניות במקום עשירות -- there is no poverty in a place of wealth: the Mishkan did not make do with a small stove
מיתיבי: אחד נותן את האבן ואחד נותן את הטיט -- הנותן את הטיט חייב! -- only the one who adds mortar is liable, not the one who sets the stone

answered_by.gloss_en: ולטעמיך, אימא סיפא: רבי יוסי ... אפילו העלה והניח על גבי דימוס -- חייב! אלא תלתא בנייני הוו -- the baraita's own seifa obligates mere placement, so it distinguishes rows: the bottom needs setting and earth (where Shmuel's setting suffices, by implication), the middle mortar, the top mere placement
